purpose: Assess only metadata-level Development/Train task-family overlap for the v3-selected fresh candidate vllm-project/vllm#64830. This is a new candidate after the prior selected identities; it is not a substitution or reuse of either prior selection.
hypothesis: The selected VLLM configuration-runner change is a distinct task family from the hash-bound previously exposed Development and Train tasks, allowing independent source qualification to be considered if the metadata review finds no direct overlap.

candidate.family_hypothesis: Move V2-only unsupported-feature checks into the V1 model-runner configuration validation path.
candidate.metadata_source: The v3 selection record and v4 frozen metadata screen only. Do not fetch PR body, discussion, patch, source, tests, prompt, or grader assets.

criteria: The same repository and pull-request number is a direct identity overlap.
The same named behavior, bug mechanism, or affected source/test family is direct family overlap.
A shared repository or broad engineering theme alone is not sufficient to declare family overlap.
Ambiguous metadata or missing exposure provenance must be classified as INSUFFICIENT_METADATA or POSSIBLE_FAMILY_OVERLAP, not as proven independence.
Public pretraining exposure remains UNKNOWN regardless of the metadata result.

heldout_handling.authorization: No Held-Out task or artifact may be inspected, identified, reported, or used.
heldout_handling.filter_rule: For any mixed-split record, inspect only the split field first; discard every row not explicitly marked Development/dev or Train/train before reading repository, PR, task ID, family, title, paths, or other identity metadata.
heldout_handling.output_rule: Do not emit Held-Out identities, titles, paths, family names, counts, or hashes of individual Held-Out assets.

stop_rules: Verify every frozen input hash before formal review; stop on any mismatch.
Do not inspect or report Held-Out identities or assets; apply the split filter before reading identity fields.
Do not fetch PR body, discussion, patch, source, tests, task prompt, grader artifacts, or hidden test outputs.
If the candidate is overlapping or metadata is insufficient, preserve that outcome and do not substitute another candidate under this protocol.
A no-overlap metadata result authorizes only a later separately frozen source-qualification protocol; it does not authorize assignment or inference.
limitations: Metadata cannot establish semantic independence as strongly as source-level task-family review.
Absence of a prior family match is not evidence of pretraining independence.
The selected candidate remains unqualified and unassigned after this review.
